record.final_answer:
Four SKUs need reordering:

| SKU | Stock (all warehouses) | Reorder level |
|---|---|---|
| BX-100 | 23 (north 14 + south 9) | 25 |
| CL-310 | 5 (north 3 + south 2) | 5 |
| EN-512 | 0 | 10 |
| GH-118 | 7 | 12 |

CL-310 is included because it sits exactly at its level, and the script flags stock that is at or below the level. The other three SKUs are above their levels: BX-220 has 40 against 30, DR-045 has 120 against 80, and FT-760 has 33 against 20.

The script failed on its first run with `column 'sku' not found`. The portal writes the file with a byte-order mark (an invisible marker at the start), so the script read the first column name as `\ufeffsku` instead of `sku`. I didn't change the export or `restock.py`. I re-ran it with the script's own encoding option, which ignores that marker:

```
python3 restock.py exports/stock-2026-10-27.csv --encoding utf-8-sig
```

I saved this as a pitfall in memcue so future runs use the right encoding from the start.
